globalTables.reason: The list of tenants is what a tenant context is chosen from and carries the MSP hierarchy, so it cannot hold a tenant_id or an RLS policy (ADR-0002). Any tenant transaction can read it, so only its owning package may name it in SQL.

The job queue must be claimable across every tenant's work, so a job row cannot sit under a per-tenant RLS policy; tenant_id is null only for a registered platform kind. The jobs_guard trigger makes the database refuse a job enqueued for a tenant other than the transaction's context (ADR-0001 E3, ADR-0002 Jobs row, DM-43). Any tenant transaction can read it, so only its owning package may name it in SQL.

Platform leases give exclusive, expiring ownership of singleton work that runs over every tenant (the job rescuer and cleaner, later schedulers), so a lease row has no tenant_id and no RLS (ADR-0002 Jobs row, DM-06). Any tenant transaction can read it, so only its owning package may name it in SQL.

The rate limiter meters a principal at chain step 10, before any tenant transaction exists, and the budget must hold across every node, so a bucket row has no RLS policy; the tenant is part of its key text (ADR-0002 rule 6, DM-07, TM-TB2-T7). Any tenant transaction can read it, so only its owning package may name it in SQL.

The installation-scope data key (T-0715, ADR-0008) seals installation secrets that belong to no tenant, such as the fleet server CA's private key, so its row has no tenant_id and no RLS (ADR-0002 rule 4). wrapped_dek is the AEAD blob a key provider returned; the runtime role can only SELECT and INSERT. Any tenant transaction can read it, so only its owning package may name it in SQL.

The update verifier's rollback floor is install-level: one monotone row shared by the server, connector and agent update paths, read before and outside any tenant transaction, so it has no tenant_id and no RLS. The guard trigger refuses any lowering and the runtime role cannot DELETE or TRUNCATE it (ENH-07, TM-D12 rule 2). Any tenant transaction can read it, so only its owning package may name it in SQL.

securityDefiner.reason: Reads every tenant's public CA certificates for the gateway client-CA pool, which fleet_ca's FORCE row-level security would show a platform-scope caller as empty. Owned by the dedicated NOLOGIN NOBYPASSRLS role activediq_catrust, which holds SELECT on tenant_id, id, state, cert_der, spki_sha256 and not_after only (never sealed_key) and one policy limited to active and retired rows; the function refuses any tenant context (42501), returns no key column, and EXECUTE is granted to activediq_app alone (T-0712, T-0733; TM-A11, TM-D24).

Destroys a retired audit checkpoint key's sealed private key. The runtime role has no UPDATE on audit_checkpoint_key (append-only, DM-80.I2), so the one allowed change runs with the owner's rights; the function takes the tenant only from app.tenant_id (row-level security still applies), refuses the newest key and a key without a committed retirement event, and the table's update trigger refuses any other change (ADR-0005 rule 11, T-0305).

platformPaths.reason: The gateway's client-CA pool holds every tenant's CA certificates, so one read runs in platform scope and calls the SECURITY DEFINER function fleet_ca_trust_anchors(), the only path to those rows: its owner role can read public certificate columns only, never sealed_key, and the function refuses a tenant context (T-0712, T-0733; TM-A11, TM-D24). It parses the tenant IDs the function returns from fleet_ca rows into typed IDs; it grants no access with them and a per-tenant check of the leaf's issuer still runs on every RPC (TM-Q8).
First-run bootstrap creates the install's first tenant before any tenant exists, so it runs outside a tenant context under WithPlatform and mints the tenant ID (ADR-0002 rules 4 and 5).

The Entra attestation callback is an unauthenticated redirect from the IdP, so no principal carries a tenant. The state the start step issued begins with the tenant it was issued for; the callback parses that prefix only to choose whose attempt table to read. The lookup is by the SHA-256 of the whole state under that tenant's RLS, so a forged or other-tenant prefix finds nothing and grants nothing. The ID is never used as an identity or authorisation input (ADR-0002 rule 5; T-0504; needs security-architect review).

Start-up compiles the report datasets against the public schema catalogue (pg_class, pg_attribute) before the install tenant exists, so the read runs outside a tenant context under WithPlatform. The catalogue is identical for every tenant and holds names and types only, never a tenant row; the result is the immutable schema the SQL registry checks identifiers against (T-1104).
Claim must see every tenant's runnable jobs, so it runs outside a tenant context under WithPlatform; the caller then runs each body in the job's own tenant (ADR-0002 Jobs row).
The rescuer re-queues running jobs of any tenant whose claim lapsed, so it runs under WithPlatform (ADR-0002 Jobs row).
The cleaner deletes finished jobs of any tenant after their retention period, so it runs under WithPlatform (ADR-0002 Jobs row).
A platform lease guards work over every tenant, so its table is registered global and the statement runs under WithPlatform (ADR-0002 Jobs row, DM-06).

The limiter meters a principal before any tenant transaction exists, and its shared bucket table is registered global, so the single upsert runs under WithPlatform (ADR-0002 rule 6, DM-07).

Test helper: runs a transaction with no tenant context to prove that connection queries outside WithTenant fail with ErrNoTenant (DM-10, T-0099 acceptance 4).

The tenant is read from the request context that the authority chain set (authority.TenantFrom), never from a request field; the parse only converts that server-set value to the typed ID for the connection lookup and fails closed (ADR-0002 rule 5).

authz.Membership receives the tenant as a string from the authorizer, which took it from the authenticated principal set by the authority chain, never from a request field; the parse only converts that server-set value to the typed ID and fails closed with ErrNoTenant (ADR-0002 rule 5).

The tenant is read from the request context that the authority chain's authentication step set (authority.TenantFrom), never from a request field; the parse only converts that server-set value to the typed ID and fails closed (ADR-0002 rule 5).

The tenant is read from the SAN of a leaf certificate the server's own CA issued and that the TLS handshake has already verified; a client cannot choose it, and the value must round-trip to its canonical form (ADR-0002 rule 5, DM-12).

Enrollment-token redemption runs before any identity exists, so the routing tenant is the prefix of the presented token. It is a request value, but it is only a lookup hint and grants nothing: the token is accepted only if the SHA-256 of the whole token (tenant prefix included) matches an unused row visible under that tenant's row-level security, and every failure is the same ErrTokenInvalid. Registered for security-architect review (ADR-0002 rule 5, DM-12.I2).

Test: runs a transaction with no tenant context to prove that the Template and NamingFormat stores refuse it with ErrNoTenant before any SQL (DM-50, DM-51). It is in a _test.go file and ships in no binary.

Test: proves the registered SECURITY DEFINER audit_wipe_retired_key refuses a call made with no tenant context (SQLSTATE 42501), which needs a transaction under WithPlatform. It is in a _test.go file and ships in no binary (ADR-0005 rule 11, T-0305).
Test helper: fetches the installation DEK under WithPlatform, because the installation key has no tenant context. It is in a _test.go file and ships in no binary (T-0715, ADR-0008).

Test helper: runs the installation-key call in a transaction the test rolls back under WithPlatform, because the installation key has no tenant context. It is in a _test.go file and ships in no binary (T-0715, ADR-0008).
